data.title: Make Ergo robust under parallel agent contention
data.body:
## Scope
- Make Ergo robust when multiple agents or subagents issue commands against the same .ergo directory in parallel.
- Preserve the local append-only JSONL storage model and one file-lock coordination path.
- Keep ordinary users and agents from needing their own retry loops or CLI tuning.

## Decisions
- Keep the existing single file-lock coordination model.
- Commands wait briefly for the repo lock before returning lock busy.
- Do not expose a public lock-timeout flag for this release.
- Do not write lock-holder diagnostics into .ergo/lock.
- Each mutating CLI invocation validates and appends its full logical event batch under one exclusive lock.
- list and show use the same exclusive lock while replaying, so read snapshots are coherent without a second protocol.

## Non-Goals
- No daemon, queue server, SQLite migration, stale-lock cleanup, or cross-machine locking protocol.
- No requirement that users stop launching multiple agents or subagents.
- No broad storage rewrite beyond the helpers needed for bounded waits and coherent snapshots.

## Risks Addressed
- Avoided nested lock helpers by keeping writer replay lockless inside existing lock scopes and giving reads a top-level locked wrapper.
- Kept the user-facing surface small by removing the public timeout knob and diagnostics.
- Preserved existing JSON output shapes for machine consumers.

data.body:
## Goal
- Make a specific claim resume blocked, closed, or legacy work instead of rejecting it.
- Replace the hardcoded done reminder with exact commands for every valid exit.

- A specific claim accepts `todo`, `blocked`, `done`, `canceled`, and legacy `error`.
- Claiming a task already held by the same agent is idempotent; claiming one held by another agent is a conflict.
- Claim and `doing` are written atomically and prior results and body remain intact.
- Claim JSON returns exact task-specific `next_commands` for `done`, `block`, `cancel`, and `release`.

- Claiming a done task reuses the original ID and does not drive an agent to create a duplicate.

## Goal

## Design
- Lifecycle receipts name the task ID and title, resulting state, cleared claim, appended message, attached result, and the oldest ready task when one exists. Omit lines that do not apply.
- Do not repeat the task body.
- `title`, `body`, and `move` identify the task and the resulting field or placement.

- A lifecycle receipt names the oldest currently ready task when available, so an agent can claim it directly.

data.title: Implement true non-ancestor dependency semantics
data.body:
## Goal
- Make relaxed non-ancestor dependency semantics real in readiness/blocking, not just accepted at link time.
- Preserve the v0.12 promise that leaf<->container edges are first-class.

## Context
- Current validation allows leaf->container and container->leaf edges, but readiness still relies on literal task state in ways that preserve old epic-only semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A leaf depending on a container becomes ready when that container is logically complete (all children done/canceled), not when some stored container state changes.
- Children of a container that depends on a leaf/container are blocked until the container's external deps are satisfied.
- Add end-to-end tests for: leaf->container, container->leaf, sibling/cross-container leaf deps, ancestor->descendant rejection, descendant->ancestor rejection, cycle rejection.
- Remove or simplify any readiness logic that still special-cases legacy epic behavior where the unified model can express the rule directly.

## Validation Gates
- go test ./internal/ergo/...
- go test ./cmd/ergo/...

## Goal
- Make leaf→container and container→leaf dependency edges behave correctly in readiness/blocking.
- Keep the fix surgical: no readiness rewrite, just teach the existing dep-check to understand containers.

## The Fix
In `isReady` and `isBlocked`, the dep loop checks `other.State != stateDone && other.State != stateCanceled`. When `other` is a container, its `.State` is meaningless — container completeness is derived from children. The fix:

1. In the dep loop, call `isContainer(other, graph)`.
2. If true, substitute `!isEpicComplete(other.ID, graph)` for the state check.
3. Remove `areEpicDepsComplete` — it's now redundant with the generalized dep loop.

That's it. Three lines of logic change plus deletion of a helper.

## Context
- `isReady` at graph.go:583, `isBlocked` at graph.go:611, `areEpicDepsComplete` at graph.go:652.
- The epic-deps check on lines 603-606 and 631-634 becomes unnecessary once the dep loop itself handles containers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A leaf depending on a container becomes ready only when all container children are done/canceled.
- A leaf depending on a container is blocked while any container child is incomplete.
- Children of a container whose container depends on an external task are blocked until that external dep is satisfied (existing behavior via the dep loop on the container's children — verify, don't break).
- `areEpicDepsComplete` is deleted.
- ancestor→descendant and descendant→ancestor deps remain rejected at link time (no change needed).

## Validation Gates
- go test ./internal/ergo/...
- go test ./cmd/ergo/...
- New integration tests: leaf→container readiness, container→leaf readiness, cross-container leaf deps.

data.title: Ergo 3.0: explicit lifecycle messages and symmetric dependency verbs
data.body:
## Goal
- Release Ergo 3.0 with explicit lifecycle messages, one owner for each mutable field, and symmetric dependency verbs.

## Decisions
- Only `body` may replace an existing task body.
- `done`, `block`, `cancel`, and `release` reject piped stdin.
- Lifecycle commands accept repeatable `-m, --message`; repeated values form paragraphs in one append-only lifecycle message.
- A lifecycle message is stored atomically with state, claim cleanup, and any result attachment.
- `sequence A B C` adds adjacent ordering edges; `unsequence A B C` removes those same adjacent edges.
- Remove `sequence rm` without an alias and return an actionable migration error.
- JSON `kind` matches `sequence` or `unsequence`; remove the redundant `action` field; `edges` contains only edges actually changed.
- Repeated sequence and unsequence calls are successful no-ops and append no redundant events.
- Existing v2 logs remain readable without migration. Once v3 message events are written, older binaries are not promised forward compatibility.

## Non-goals
- No generic `set`, `reopen`, `note`, or body-append command.
- No redesign of the leaf versus container `show --json` envelope in this release.
- No compatibility aliases for removed v2 syntax.

## Release standard
- Help, quickstart, spec, README, changelog, and the shipped planning skill must agree.
- Validate source-built binaries, copied v2 logs, release archives, Homebrew delivery, and the locally installed command.

data.title: Ergo 3.0: explicit commands and agent-readable output

data.body:
## Goal
- Release Ergo 3.0 with explicit lifecycle messages, symmetric dependency verbs, and one output mode designed for model comprehension.

## Decisions
- Only `body` may replace an existing task body.
- `done`, `block`, `cancel`, and `release` reject piped stdin.
- Lifecycle commands accept repeatable `-m, --message`; repeated values form paragraphs in one append-only lifecycle message.
- Drop `--summary`. A new result is identified by its path and recorded hash; any human note goes in a `-m` message.
- Preserve distinct summaries already stored in v1 or v2 result events and render them as legacy metadata; do not migrate or discard them.
- A lifecycle message is stored atomically with state, claim cleanup, and any result attachment.
- `sequence A B C` adds adjacent ordering edges; `unsequence A B C` removes those same adjacent edges.
- Remove `sequence rm` without an alias and return an actionable migration error.
- Remove the global `--json` flag and every JSON output branch. Successful commands emit one concise text representation intended for agents.
- `show` is a complete structured Markdown document; `list` is a compact readable hierarchy; `claim` shows the claimed task and exact exits.
- The claim and show text is the agent-loop contract: the task ID appears in a fixed, greppable position so an agent can carry it into the next command.
- Creation commands return generated IDs in readable form. Mutations and maintenance commands return only the concise confirmation needed to understand the postcondition.
- Keep JSON only where Ergo code consumes it: inline creation metadata and the append-only event log.
- Existing v2 logs remain readable without migration. Legacy `--json` invocations fail with an actionable instruction to rerun without the flag.
- Once v3 message events are written, older binaries are not promised forward compatibility.

## Non-goals
- No generic `set`, `reopen`, `note`, or body-append command.
- No machine-oriented output API, compatibility output mode, or duplicate text and JSON representations.
- No compatibility aliases for removed v2 syntax, including `--summary` and `sequence rm`.
- No redesign of the event-log encoding or inline creation metadata in this release.

## Release standard
- Help and quickstart are the complete manual for an agent with an empty context window; neither leans on external documentation.
- After the CLI stabilizes, review both rendered manuals from fresh eyes for accuracy, coverage, order, examples, and non-redundancy.
- Judge length by succinctness, not a fixed word count: every line must earn its place, say each thing once, and stay readable by both a human and an empty-context agent.

v0.12: Unify task/epic + simplify CLI surface
data.body:
## Scope
Drop the `task` vs `epic` kind distinction. Every entity is a task. A task becomes a container the moment it gets a child; without children it is a leaf. One-level nesting only (containers cannot themselves have a parent).

Bundle with this change: simplify the surrounding CLI surface to match.

## What changes
- Data model: drop `Kind`; `isContainer(t)` is derived from has-children.
- Containers cannot hold state/claim/results (enforced).
- Containers complete when all children are done/canceled (unchanged).
- `new epic` subcommand removed.
- `plan` command removed; bulk-create payload (`tasks: [...]`) lives on `new task`.
- `plans.jsonl` remains the source-of-truth event log even after removing the `plan` command.
- Dep rules relax: any two non-ancestor tasks may have an edge.
- `list --epics` flag removed/renamed.
- State+claim coupling reframed as one invariant in docs.
- Quickstart input-mode pedagogy trimmed.
- Repo docs outside embedded help/quickstart are swept for old surface references before release.

- Arbitrary-depth nesting (capped at one level).

- UI/output redesign beyond what the model change forces.

## Goal

data.body:
## Goal
- Convert draft-of-new-help-text.md into a precise implementation contract before code work spreads.
- Resolve any ambiguity in the draft into explicit parser and output rules so downstream tasks can be mechanical.

## Context
- The draft introduces positional JSON args for new/set/plan, stdin-as-body semantics, and a narrower field vocabulary.
- We are not preserving deleted surface as current docs; this task should lock what the new surface is, not narrate what it replaced.

## Recommended Contract Lock
- Commands:
  - `new task [json]` creates one task; stdin, when piped, is the task body.
  - `set <id> [json]` updates one task; stdin, when piped, replaces the body.
  - `plan --file <path> [json]` creates one epic plus child tasks from a markdown file.
  - `show <id>` and `list ...` keep their current read roles; `claim`, `sequence`, `init`, `where`, `prune`, and `compact` remain.
- Input model:
  - Remove `--body-stdin`, `--title`, `--body`, and other create or set metadata flags from the forward surface.
  - `new`, `set`, and `plan` accept at most one positional JSON object argument.
  - If stdin is not a TTY, read all stdin as the body payload. If stdin is a TTY, leave body unchanged unless the command creates a new task with no body.
  - Empty piped stdin is allowed: on `new task` it creates an empty body; on `set` it clears the body.
- JSON field vocabulary:
  - `new task` accepts `title`, optional `epic`, optional `state`, optional `claim`, and optional `result`.
  - `set` accepts optional `title`, `epic`, `state`, `claim`, and `result`.
  - `plan --file` accepts a JSON object for the top-level epic fields; require `title` there rather than deriving it from the file name.
  - Unknown keys are rejected with close-match suggestions.
- Result semantics:
  - `result` is the new user-facing field and is a single file path string.
  - New writes append one result entry with that path and no required summary.
  - Old logs with `result_path` and `result_summary` remain readable; show output may still display legacy summaries when present.
- Plan file semantics:
  - Split chunks on a line that is exactly `---`.
  - Each chunk must begin with a level-1 heading `# Title`.
  - The heading text becomes the child title; the remaining markdown, including blank lines, becomes the body and may be empty.
  - Dependencies are not inferred from file order; sequencing remains explicit via `sequence`.
  - Parsing is atomic: any malformed chunk aborts without writing.
- Output and read model:
  - `list --json` stays the default machine-readable inventory view; `--all` widens scope to include done and canceled items.
  - `show --json <id>` remains the one-item detail view and should continue to expose child and dependency detail.
  - Do not teach raw `.ergo` parsing in docs.
- Removed surface:
  - Old forms like JSON-on-stdin object mutation, `--body-stdin`, `new task` with `tasks:[...]`, `list --containers`, and docs that teach them should disappear from the forward manual.
  - Removed commands or flags must fail non-zero with clear errors, not fall through to help.

- Add a completion note to this task body that spells out the exact command forms for new, set, plan, list, and show.
- The note names the accepted JSON argument shapes, stdin behavior, and whether empty stdin/body is allowed for each command.
- The note lists any edge decisions that tests must lock down: malformed inline JSON, missing title, body plus JSON interactions, markdown chunk parsing, and result field behavior.
- Dependent tasks can implement against this note without re-reading the whole draft for interpretation.

- Manual review against draft-of-new-help-text.md
- Manual review against go run ./cmd/ergo --help and quickstart to identify every intentional break

data.title: v0.12 follow-up: correctness and minimalism
data.body:
## Scope
Address the correctness and minimalism gaps found in the shipped v0.12 implementation without expanding the product surface beyond the intended unified task/container model.

## Why
The current branch is directionally right, but a few behaviors still contradict the vision:
- a leaf can be promoted into a claimed/stateful container
- relaxed non-ancestor deps are accepted but not honored by readiness/blocking logic
- bulk-create still exposes legacy plan/epic vocabulary and silently ignores some user mistakes
- executable fixtures still teach removed commands

## Decisions (locked)
- Bulk-create (`new task` with `tasks:[...]`) should use unified container vocabulary in JSON output, not legacy `plan` / `epic` shape.
- Mixed bulk-create payloads should fail closed: reject top-level leaf-only mutation fields (`state`, `claim`, `result_*`, `epic`) when `tasks` is present.
- Historical proposal docs may remain if clearly labeled as proposals; executable artifacts and current-user docs must match the live CLI.

## Non-goals
- No new user-facing workflow beyond fixing the intended v0.12 model.
- No large storage migration unless it is strictly necessary for correctness.

## Success criteria
- Containers never expose leaf-only state/claim/results semantics.
- Non-ancestor dependency rules are reflected in readiness/blocking behavior, not just validation.
- Common operator mistakes around bulk-create fail with clear errors instead of being silently ignored.
- Repo fixtures and smoke coverage match the current CLI.

data.title: Relax dep rules to any non-ancestor
data.body:
## Goal
Replace the current "task↔task or epic↔epic, never cross-kind" dependency rule with: **any two non-ancestor tasks may have an edge**.

## Rule (post-change)
- An edge from A to B is valid iff: A != B; B is not an ancestor of A; A is not an ancestor of B; the resulting graph has no cycles.
- "Ancestor" under one-level nesting means: B.epic == A or A.epic == B.
- Container-to-leaf edges are explicitly supported (a container depending on a leaf blocks all of its children, mirroring today's epic-to-epic behavior).
- Leaf-to-container edges are explicitly supported (a leaf is ready only when all children of the container are done/canceled).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `validateDepKinds` is replaced (or removed and its responsibilities folded into the edge-creation path).
- New ancestor-check function rejects ancestor↔descendant edges with a clear error.
- Cycle detection continues to work across the relaxed edge set.
- New tests cover: leaf→container, container→leaf, leaf-in-A→leaf-in-B, ancestor→descendant (rejected), descendant→ancestor (rejected), self-edge (rejected), cycle (rejected).
- "Ready" computation correctly cascades: a leaf depending on a container is ready only when the container is "done" (all children done/canceled).

- New tests in `internal/ergo/dep_rules_test.go` cover the cases above
- Manual: `ergo sequence <a-leaf> <a-container>` succeeds; `ergo sequence <child> <parent>` returns ancestor error

data.title: Enforce container invariants on mutation
data.body:
## Goal
Enforce the rules that make the unified model coherent: containers cannot hold state/claim/results, and one-level nesting is preserved.

## Invariants to enforce
1. A task with at least one child (a container) cannot be mutated with `state`, `claim`, `result_path`, or `result_summary`. Attempts return a clear error.
2. A task may only be assigned as a child to a parent that itself has no parent (one-level nesting cap).
3. A task may not become a parent (i.e., have a child assigned to it via `epic` field) if it currently has `state != todo` or a non-empty `claim`. This prevents a leaf with in-flight work from being silently promoted to a container.
4. When a task becomes a container (gains its first child), any future direct state/claim mutation is rejected per rule 1.
5. When a container loses its last child (all children deleted/pruned), it becomes a leaf again and direct state mutation is permitted.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New rejection paths in `set` and `new task --epic <id>` for the above cases.
- Error messages cite the invariant violated (e.g., "cannot set state on a container task; containers complete when all children complete").
- Unit tests for each invariant: state-on-container rejected; claim-on-container rejected; child-of-child rejected; promotion of doing/claimed leaf rejected.
- Existing tests still pass.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...` passes
- New tests in `internal/ergo/state_machine_test.go` or a new file covering each numbered invariant above

data.body:
## Goal
- Replace `ergo plan` with `ergo new epic`, using a positional title and `--file`.

## Context
- `plan` creates a parent plus children from a markdown file (`internal/ergo/plan_input.go`).
- Under the Ergo 4 vocabulary the parent is an "epic", and creation lives under the `new` verb.

## Design
- Usage: `ergo new epic "<title>" --file <path>`. Title positional; `--file` carries the child chunks.
- The file format is unchanged: `# Title` chunks separated by a line that is exactly `---`.
- No JSON envelope.
- Retire `plan`: keep it only as a hidden alias or a one-line migration error pointing to `new epic`. Pick one and state which.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `ergo new epic "Authentication" --file tasks.md` creates an epic with the file's children.
- Inline JSON is no longer accepted.
- Missing title, empty `--file`, and malformed chunks fail clearly.
- `ergo plan ...` either aliases to `new epic` or emits a clear migration message; the choice is documented.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...`
- `ergo new epic "T" --file tasks.md`, then `ergo list --epic <id>`.

## Goal
- Replace `ergo plan` with `ergo new epic` while preserving useful bulk-creation behavior.

## Design
- Usage: `ergo new epic "<title>" --file <path>`.
- `--file` is required and must contain at least one valid `# Title` chunk separated by a line that is exactly `---`.
- Optional piped stdin is the epic body. No pipe produces an empty epic body.
- Epics remain derived from having children; Ergo does not create an empty epic.
- The markdown child-file format and file-order semantics are unchanged.
- Successful output names the epic ID and title, every child ID and title, and the task and dependency counts.
- `plan` is removed rather than aliased.

- The success output gives agents every created ID without an extra list or show call.
- No JSON input is accepted.

## Goal
Rewrite `internal/ergo/help.txt` to reflect the unified model and simplified surface. Must remain a complete cold-start reference for agents.

## Must-change sections
- Top paragraph: replace "Epics contain tasks" framing. New framing: "Tasks form a graph. A task with children is a container (colloquially: an epic). Containers complete when their children do."

- FLAGS FOR new/set: keep `--epic <id>` but reword description: "assign or reassign to parent task (\"\" to unassign). One-level nesting only."

- STATE: reframe the state+claim coupling rules as one invariant: **claim and `doing` move together** - claiming sets `doing`; finishing (`done` or `canceled`) drops the claim; `error` retains the claim; `blocked` is orthogonal.
- Dep rules note: "deps allowed between any two non-ancestor tasks; cycles forbidden."
- Bulk-create: a one-line example showing `new task` with a `tasks: [...]` payload (replacing what `plan` used to do).

## Acceptance Criteria
- 100% surface coverage preserved (no removed command or flag goes undocumented; no remaining command or flag is missing).

- Length comparable to current (not bloated; not lossy).

data.title: Redesign task creation input
data.body:
## Goal
- Replace the inline JSON envelope on `ergo new task` with a positional title and one flag.

## Context
- Today `new task` parses `{title, epic, state, claim, result}` in `internal/ergo/cli_input.go`.
- The envelope holds only flat scalars, so JSON adds no structure; a positional title and a flag express the same thing more legibly.
- Bodies keep arriving on stdin.

## Design
- Usage: `ergo new task "<title>" [--epic <id>]`. The title is a required positional operand, matching `title <id> <title>` and `show <id>`.
- Keep `--epic <id>` as the only optional creation flag.
- Drop `state`, `claim`, and `result` from creation. Each is reachable by composing verbs, e.g. `ergo claim $(ergo new task "X") --agent me` or `ergo block $(ergo new task "X") -m "..."`.
- `new task` prints only the bare task ID to stdout, so it composes inside a subshell. Treat this as an invariant.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `ergo new task "Add login"` creates a todo leaf and prints just its ID.
- `--epic <id>` places the task under an epic; an unknown epic fails clearly.
- Inline JSON is no longer accepted on `new task`.
- `state`, `claim`, and `result` are not creation inputs.
- Optional stdin still sets the initial body; empty or no pipe leaves it empty.

## Validation Gates
- `go test ./...`
- `ergo new task "X"`, then `ergo show <id>`: confirm a todo leaf and bare-ID output.

## Goal
- Replace the inline JSON envelope on `ergo new task` with a positional title and one optional placement flag.

## Design
- Usage: `ergo new task "<title>" [--epic <id>]`.

- `--epic <id>` accepts an existing epic or a clean, unclaimed root todo task with no results; the latter becomes an epic on its first child.
- Creation always yields an unclaimed todo. State, claim, messages, and results belong to later lifecycle verbs.
- Successful creation prints only the bare task ID to stdout so shell and agent composition remain reliable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `ergo new task "Add login"` creates an unclaimed todo leaf and prints only its six-character ID.
- `--epic <id>` preserves existing placement and first-child promotion rules.
- Unknown, nested, claimed, closed, or result-bearing destinations fail clearly.
- Optional piped stdin sets the initial body; empty or absent stdin produces an empty body.
- Creation no longer accepts state, claim, result, or an inline JSON envelope.

- Compose `ergo show "$(ergo new task "X")"` and confirm bare-ID stdout.

data.body:
## Goal
- Make every Ergo command observe and commit one coherent backlog transaction, including across crashes, short writes, and concurrent processes.

## Decisions
- Preserve the append-only JSONL backlog.
- Represent one logical mutation as one versioned transaction record.
- Repair an incomplete final record before a later append and sync committed data before reporting success.
- Fail closed when multiple supported log filenames coexist.
- Fail closed on unknown or structurally invalid events; compaction must never erase data it cannot interpret.

## Scope
- Repository discovery, locking, transaction framing, durability, replay validation, migration of every read and write path, result evidence, and immutable compatibility fixtures.
- Continue reading supported legacy standalone event records and legacy log filenames when exactly one log exists.

## Non-goals
- Do not replace JSONL with a database or daemon.
- Do not introduce distributed locking or weaken the existing project-local advisory lock.

## Goal
- Ensure attached results are stable regular files inside the resolved project and record Git provenance correctly across repository layouts.

## Context
- Resolve the project root and result target through symlinks, then verify containment.
- Reject directories, FIFOs, devices, sockets, and other non-regular files.

data.body:
## Goal
- Give agents a supported, lossless way to read the current body before preserving, editing, or migrating it.

## Decisions
- Add `ergo show <id> --body` as a field projection within Ergo’s single readable output mode.
- Emit exactly the current body bytes. Do not synthesize YAML front matter, a title heading, dependencies, messages, results, epic children, ANSI, or a trailing newline.
- For an epic, project the epic body only. For an empty body, succeed with zero stdout bytes.
- Keep ordinary `ergo show <id>` output unchanged.
- Do not restore JSON output and do not add content heuristics to `ergo body`; Markdown that resembles rendered output remains valid literal body content.

## Scope
- Typed query outcome, Cobra flag, exact renderer behavior, black-box compatibility coverage, manuals, stable specification, README guidance, and changelog.

## Validation Strategy
- Exact projection and pipeline idempotence: focused application and CLI tests, owned by the implementation task and run with that change.
- Public command and documentation contract: manual/help tests plus `task ci`, owned by the documentation task and run after implementation.

## Integration
- Implement after the application and CLI architecture wave so the feature targets the final typed query, renderer, stream, and Cobra boundaries.
- Finish the feature contract before final architecture reconciliation so maintainer documentation describes the resulting public surface once.

## Non-goals
- Do not make the complete `show` document round-trippable.
- Do not add body projections to `claim`, `list`, or lifecycle commands.
